editorial.thesis: A hospitality-and-motor-trade city of about 289,000. Its retail is heavy on desserts, sweets & ice cream and restaurants & fast food, and thin on coaching & training and pharmacy & health retail — and 35% of residents live in zones with under 60% of the city's average retail depth.
takeaways: Branded retail is about 38% of Bengaluru's. 24.23 chain outlets per lakh residents against 63.31 in Bengaluru; 31 of the 51 national brands we track are present, led by Apollo Pharmacy 12, Reliance Trends 6, Domino's 5.

The mapped economy leans to hotels & stays. Shares of all mapped places: hotels & stays 8.7% (Bengaluru 4.0%); automotive 4.6% (Bengaluru 2.8%); offices 6.3% (Bengaluru 12.7%); healthcare 4.8% (Bengaluru 7.7%). Raw counts would mislead because Bengaluru is mapped more completely (108,499 places against 2,445), so we compare mix, not counts.
Supply and demand are misaligned. 4 zones hold 35% of residents with under 60% of the city's average retail depth. Ambalapadi alone has about 29,000 residents and 10 mapped food & drink places.
Retail is more concentrated than in Bengaluru. 57% of commercial places sit in the busiest tenth of the city (Bengaluru 40%). The largest cores are Courts (536 places) and Manipal (346).

The widest brand gaps against Bengaluru. Apollo Pharmacy 12 outlets vs 283; MedPlus 3 outlets vs 273; Café Coffee Day 3 outlets vs 221. These are leads to check against live listings, not verdicts: a brand may trade under another name or have opened since the map was updated.

numbers.title: The city in eight numbers
numbers.deck: A 6 km circle around the centre, processed with the same rules as Bengaluru, so every comparison is like for like. Where raw counts would mislead — because a bigger city is mapped more completely — we compare shares and mix instead.

map.title: Where people live, where shops are
map.deck: Switch layers. The amber “gap” layer is the one to study: it marks places with many residents but little retail around them. Hover any hexagon (about 0.1 km²) for its numbers; click a zone on the right to isolate it.

captions.residents: Where people live. Courts and Kunjibettu are the largest zones by residents (75,000 and 43,000). Modelled residents per square kilometre.
captions.supply: Where the shops are. The busiest tenth of cells hold 57% of all commercial places, and Courts alone lists 536.
captions.chains: Where the brands are. Manipal holds 24 of the 70 tracked chain outlets, and Courts adds 23.
captions.education: Where the campuses are. Manipal and Courts lead on education places (71 and 37, with 17 and 7 coaching centres) — a daytime youth market that residents alone do not show.
captions.gap: The gap. Amber: many residents nearby, little retail. Blue: far more retail than local residents explain — the commercial cores that draw people in. The deepest amber sits in Ambalapadi and Santhekatte. The blue cores include Courts.

zones.title: Zone by zone, by PIN code
zones.deck: Each zone is a postal-code area. Residents are modelled counts; places are mapped businesses and services. “Retail depth” is places per 10,000 residents — the tick marks the city average. Click a row to see it on the map.

mix.title: What the retail layer is made of
mix.deck: Raw counts per resident would favour whichever city is mapped more completely (108,499 places in Bengaluru against 2,445 here). So this compares each category's share of all mapped places. 100 means the same share as Bengaluru; below 100 is thinner, above is stronger.
mix.note: Against Bengaluru, Udupi's mapped places over-index on hotels & stays (8.7% vs 4.0%), automotive (4.6% vs 2.8%), food & beverage (12.2% vs 9.8%) and under-index on offices (6.3% vs 12.7%), healthcare (4.8% vs 7.7%), services & crafts (4.9% vs 6.6%).

chains.title: Who is mapped here, and who is not
chains.deck: 70 outlets of 31 tracked national brands within 6 km — 24.23 per lakh residents against Bengaluru's 63.31 (2535 outlets of 51 brands). Filled names have at least one mapped outlet (count shown); dashed names have none.
chains.note: Read dashed names as leads, not verdicts. “No mapped outlet” can mean a brand trades under a different listed name, or has opened since the map was updated. The widest gaps against Bengaluru are Apollo Pharmacy (12 vs 283); MedPlus (3 vs 273); Café Coffee Day (3 vs 221). Premium reports check every lead against live listings.

formats.title: Which formats have room
formats.deck: 9 formats, thinnest first. The index is the format's share of all mapped places relative to Bengaluru's, so low means thin by Bengaluru's standard. “Where to look” ranks zones with at least 40,000 residents by residents per mapped outlet — a first-pass screen for where one more outlet would face the least local competition.

people.title: Who the customers are
people.deck: Age mix inside the 6 km circle, from Meta's age rasters (modelled, not a census).
people.note: Udupi's age mix against Bengaluru: children (0–14) 18.0% vs 22.8%, 15–24 18.0% vs 19.5%, working age 50.8% vs 50.2%, 60+ 13.1% vs 7.5%. Under-25s are 36% of residents.

zones.576102: Reasonably supplied: 164 places for about 43,000 residents (index 63), 14 chain outlets.

restaurants.read: Restaurants & fast food are 8.8% of mapped places against 7.0% in Bengaluru — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Domino's 5 (Bengaluru 193), KFC 4 (Bengaluru 83), Pizza Hut 4 (Bengaluru 99), Burger King 2 (Bengaluru 34).
restaurants.watch: Independent eateries are numerous and unevenly mapped. Treat the index as a screen and confirm competitor density street by street.

cafes.read: Cafés, tea & coffee are 2.7% of mapped places against 2.6% in Bengaluru, so the mix is level. Mapped chain outlets: Café Coffee Day 3 (Bengaluru 221), Starbucks 1 (Bengaluru 42), Chai Point 1 (Bengaluru 50).
cafes.watch: Chai stalls and independent cafés are under-mapped. A café concept here competes on price and habit as much as on novelty.

desserts.read: Desserts, sweets & ice cream are 1.1% of mapped places against 0.8% in Bengaluru — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Baskin Robbins 1 (Bengaluru 67), Naturals 1 (Bengaluru 18).
desserts.watch: Traditional sweet shops are the real benchmark and sit outside most chain lists.

grocery.read: Grocery & daily needs are 2.5% of mapped places against 2.5% in Bengaluru, so the mix is level. Mapped chain outlets: Reliance Smart / Fresh 3 (Bengaluru 64), More 2 (Bengaluru 30), Big Bazaar 1 (Bengaluru 18), Vishal Mega Mart 1 (Bengaluru 11).
grocery.watch: Neighbourhood kirana stores are the real incumbents and the least completely mapped outlets, so any gap is overstated. Test a site against local store density before acting.

pharmacy.read: Pharmacy & health retail are 0.9% of mapped places against 1.4% in Bengaluru — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Apollo Pharmacy 12 (Bengaluru 283), MedPlus 3 (Bengaluru 273), Wellness Forever 2 (Bengaluru 6).
pharmacy.watch: Independent chemists are dense and lightly mapped. Hospital and clinic clusters are the natural anchors.

apparel.read: Apparel, footwear & jewellery are 4.8% of mapped places against 5.1% in Bengaluru, so the mix is level. Mapped chain outlets: Reliance Trends 6 (Bengaluru 146), Bata 2 (Bengaluru 130), Westside 1 (Bengaluru 20), Pantaloons 1 (Bengaluru 18).
apparel.watch: Established multi-brand traders and local bazaars sit behind these numbers; new entrants compete with them as well as with chains.

banking.read: Banks & ATMs are 7.4% of mapped places against 6.6% in Bengaluru — above its share.
banking.watch: This category includes insurance and agency offices, so it overstates branch banking. Use it as a signal of commercial activity, not a branch count.

coaching.read: Coaching & training are 1.4% of mapped places against 2.4% in Bengaluru — below its share.
coaching.watch: Coaching demand follows the exam calendar. Formats that depend on it should be tested across the academic year.

fitness.read: Fitness & wellness are 2.5% of mapped places against 3.8% in Bengaluru — below its share.
fitness.watch: Gym listings change often and are inconsistently categorised; verify before drawing conclusions.
